messages:
Sara M.: Heads up — getting a bunch of escalations from support: p95/p99 latency for /v1/generate jumped ~3x for a handful of high-volume customers starting ~08:10 UTC. Ticket IDs: #4532, #4537. Saw errors in one report but mostly just long tail latency. @oncall-bot kicked in.

Mike K.: I see the same in dashboards. redwood_request_duration_seconds_p95 jumped from 120ms->360ms; p99 from 420ms->1.2s for model=llama-13b-prod in us-west-2. Timing lines up with a deploy at 08:05 (deploy-bot shows rollout to 20% then to 100%). :eyes: 

Raj P.: Early hypothesis: prefix/KV cache miss rate spiked. redwood_cache_prefix_miss_total went from 2% -> 48% around the same time. That would explain token-level latency increases. I'm pulling cache stats.

deploy-bot: rollout redwood/serving-runtime@sha256:7f9a2 applied at 08:05 UTC to non-canary pools -> full.

Sara M.: Support reported repro steps (minimal):
1) POST /v1/generate model=llama-13b-prod with same prompt repeatedly
2) p95 stable previously, now first few requests are fast then later ones slow again

Leo S.: Running quick check on node cache metrics (us-west-2 pool):
```
$ rd-cachectl stats --pool us-west-2 --model llama-13b-prod --prefix
prefix_entries_total: 215k
prefix_kv_bytes: 7.9GB
prefix_miss_rate: 0.47
eviction_rate_per_min: 1200
hot_prefixes: 820
```
Eviction rate massively up vs baseline ~30/min.

Alisa R.: Suspicious — eviction rate + miss rate combo = thrash. Could be cache key churn or a bug in the eviction policy in this deploy. Any code changes touching prefix cache key generation in the PR? @Mike K.

Mike K.: Yes, PR 8124 changed cache key generation to include `session_id` to avoid cross-session prefix reuse. Patch excerpt:
```
# old: key = f"{model}:{prompt_hash}:{prefix_len}"
# new: key = f"{model}:{prompt_hash}:{session_id}:{prefix_len}"
```
That created a higher cardinality key space. I thought it would reduce cross-tenant pollution but didn't account for ephemeral session IDs.

Raj P.: That will definitely increase unique keys and reduce hit rate — causing cold prefixes and eviction thrash. Also found a second issue: whitespace normalization was inconsistent across SDK v2 and v3 so same prompt hashed differently.

Sara M.: So two contributors: session_id in key + inconsistent normalizer -> much higher cardinality -> evictions -> p99 spike. Concrete mitigations?

Alisa R.: Short term (minutes): revert session_id change or patch to drop ephemeral session_id from prefix keys. We can also increase cache capacity and throttle eviction to reduce thrash while we patch.

Leo S.: Immediate ops commands I'd run now:
1) Pause full rollout: roll back runtime to previous stable sha or halt ingest to affected pools.
```
$ deployctl rollback redwood/serving-runtime --to-sha sha256:2a4b...
```
2) Increase prefix cache size on hot nodes (temporary):
```
$ rd-admin set-config --pool us-west-2 --model llama-13b-prod --prefix-cache-size 12GB
```
3) Flip eviction policy to LFU for 30 minutes to prefer keeping frequently accessed prefixes.
```
$ rd-admin set-config --pool us-west-2 --evict-policy LFU
```
Note: these are stopgap — we should deploy proper code fix asap.

Mike K.: I'll open a rollback PR now and also prepare a minimal fix that keeps `session_id` out of the cache key but preserves isolation for authenticated tenants by switching to `tenant_id` (stable) + normalized prompt hash. Patch snippet:
```
- key = f"{model}:{prompt_hash}:{session_id}:{prefix_len}"
+ # use tenant_id (stable) instead of session_id to avoid ephemeral churn
+ key = f"{model}:{tenant_id}:{norm_prompt_hash}:{prefix_len}"
```
Also adding a normalization step (avoid regex for clarity):
```
# collapse whitespace and lowercase
norm_prompt = " ".join(prompt.split()).strip().lower()
norm_prompt_hash = sha256(norm_prompt.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
```

Raj P.: I ran a quick sim locally with patch and cache hit rate recovers to ~86% for our hot prompt corpus. I'll bundle unit tests for normalization mismatch.

Sara M.: Support wants an ETA for customers. We should canary fix on 10% traffic then scale. Proposed timeline:
- T+0m: pause rollout / short rollback (ops) — DONE? (Leo)
- T+10m: deploy hotfix branch to canary (10% traffic)
- T+30m: monitor p95/p99 and cache_miss metrics
- T+60m: full rollout if green

Leo S.: Rollback initiated at 08:20 UTC to sha256:2a4b... — confirming nodes are back to baseline config. After rollback, prefix_miss dropped from 47% -> 6% over ~7 minutes, p99 trending down. :thumbsup: 

support-bot: Notifying affected customers with templated message (escalation category: latency; status: investigating -> partial mitigation applied)

Mike K.: Hotfix branch ready: redwood/serving-runtime@fix/kv-key-tenant-id. Will push to canary cluster now.

deploy-bot: applying redwood/serving-runtime@fix/kv-key-tenant-id to canary (10%) at 08:33 UTC.

Raj P.: Prom queries to watch during canary:
- Cache miss rate: sum(rate(redwood_cache_prefix_miss_total[1m])) by (pool)
- Eviction rate: sum(rate(redwood_cache_eviction_total[1m])) by (pool)
- p99 latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))

Alisa R.: After canary for 15m: prefix_miss on canary nodes dropped to 4% and p99 for canary back to baseline. Non-canary still healing from rollback but trending down. Good sign.

Sara M.: What about longer-term fixes so we don't hit this again?

Mike K.: Action items (long-term):
- Revert session_id logic permanently and adopt tenant-scoped keys (PR merged)
- Add strict normalization library shared across SDKs and runtime (to avoid cross-SDK hashing mismatch)
- Add test harness that simulates high-cardinality session churn to detect cache thrash in CI
- Telemetry alert: add an alert for sudden increase in prefix_miss_rate > 15% over 5m and eviction_rate > 200/min
- Consider adaptive cache sizing and LFU hybrid eviction to tolerate bursty patterns

Raj P.: Also documenting root cause in postmortem: stamp key points and timeline + customer impact + code snippet of offending change. I'll own the postmortem draft.

Sara M.: Customer outreach: Support will send updated status and ETA (<2h for full remediation). I'll coordinate with CSMs for impacted enterprise customers.

Leo S.: Follow up: we should run a backfill to prewarm prefixes for top 1000 prompts used by affected customers to avoid cold start after full rollout.

Alisa R.: Noted — I'll create job to prewarm using recorded requests. Command:
```
$ rd-prewarm --model llama-13b-prod --prompts-file hot_prompts_top1k.txt --parallel 64
```

Sara M.: Summary / next steps:
- Immediate: rollback applied, canary hotfix running -> metrics improving
- Short-term: merge hotfix, full rollout after 1h of stable canary
- Medium-term: normalization lib, test harness, alerting, prewarm job
- Owners: Raj (postmortem + tests), Mike (fix + SDK coord), Leo (ops & prewarm), Alisa (alerts)

Sara M.: I'll keep thread updated. Thanks all. :heart:
